title: Passing to a method
cards/0/body:
When you call a method, each argument is copied into its parameter.

For a struct, the whole struct is copied. For a class, only the reference: the method gets the address of the same object.
cards/1/task: Step through the call to Move in both versions.
cards/1/variants/struct/steps/0/note: p is a struct in Main's frame.
cards/1/variants/struct/steps/1/note: Move got a copy of the whole struct.
cards/1/variants/struct/steps/2/note: We change the copy in Move's frame.
cards/1/variants/struct/steps/3/note: Move's frame is gone, and the copy with it.
cards/1/variants/class/steps/0/note: p is a reference to an object on the heap.
cards/1/variants/class/steps/1/note: Move got a copy of the reference, to the same object.
cards/1/variants/class/steps/2/note: We change the object on the heap, shared by p and q.
cards/1/variants/class/steps/3/note: Move's frame is gone; the object stays modified.
cards/2/q: Point is a struct. What does the program print?
cards/2/explain: Move changed its own copy. The variable p in Main stayed the same.
cards/3/body:
With ref, the method gets not a copy but access to the caller's variable.

out is the same, but the method must assign a value (like in int.TryParse).
in passes by reference, but read-only: a big struct doesn't have to be copied.
cards/3/deep: in with a regular (non-readonly) struct can force the compiler to make "defensive copies" when calling its methods, in case a method changes fields. That's why big structs are declared readonly struct.
cards/4/task: Now Move(ref p). See what q points to.
cards/4/steps/0/note: p is a struct in Main's frame.
cards/4/steps/1/note: q is not a copy but a reference to the variable p in Main.
cards/4/steps/2/note: p itself changes, right in Main's frame.
cards/5/q: Point is a class, p = (5, 5). What is p.X after Reset(p)?
cards/5/explain: The method replaced its own copy of the reference with a new object. The variable p still leads to the old object. To replace p, you need ref.
cards/5/wrong/1: That would happen with ref Point q. Without ref, the method only changes its own copy of the reference.
cards/6/task: Check it on the rig: what happens to q inside Reset.
cards/6/steps/1/note: q is a copy of the reference p.
cards/6/steps/2/note: q now leads to a new object. p still leads to the old one.
cards/6/steps/3/note: Reset's frame is gone. The new object became garbage, and p didn't change.
cards/7/q: Match each modifier to its meaning
cards/7/pairs/0/1: The method reads and changes the caller's variable
cards/7/pairs/1/1: The method must assign a value
cards/8/q: Why pass a big struct as in?
cards/8/options/0: To avoid copying it on every call and to forbid changes
cards/8/options/1: So the method can change it
cards/8/options/2: So it moves to the heap
cards/8/explain: in passes an address instead of copying every field, and the compiler won't let the method change it.
